predictions.reasoning: A sharp jump in the implied probability that Xi Jinping is removed from power before 2027 would signal acute political instability at the top of the CCP. Political succession crises in an authoritarian one-party state are deeply disruptive to policy continuity, capital controls, and investor confidence. Chinese equities carry a large political-risk premium; a credible leadership-crisis signal would trigger heavy foreign outflows and a sharp risk-off move in the most liquid China proxy (FXI). The magnitude could easily exceed 700bps because such an event is tail-risk with no priced-in expectation. Direction is unambiguously negative in the short term regardless of whether markets later view a successor as reformist.

predictions.reasoning: A leadership-crisis signal would spark capital-flight fears and pressure the yuan lower. FX is a natural safe-haven-flow channel; USDCNH would spike higher (yuan weaker). CYB is a liquid but relatively insensitive proxy — the PBOC manages the fixing tightly, which dampens moves, so the 12h magnitude likely stays below the 700bps tradable threshold. Direction is negative but the proxy is a weak, managed instrument.

evidence_used: Market question implies a discrete political-risk event (removal of Xi Jinping) with a very low base rate
China equities (FXI/KWEB) and the yuan carry a large embedded political/policy-continuity premium
Authoritarian succession crises historically produce sharp short-term risk-off moves in affected markets
Polymarket probability shifts on low-liquidity political questions are frequently noise rather than leaked information
uncertainty_notes: The base rate of Xi being removed is extremely low; most probability spikes will be noise or manipulation, not genuine leaks
If a spike is not corroborated by credible reporting within hours, both the market and any asset move likely reverse
Direction of equities is clear (down) on instability, but a market could later reinterpret a successor as reform-positive, muddying the 12h signal
Yuan proxy (CYB) is heavily managed by the PBOC, weakening its usefulness as a signal channel

llm_justification.summary: A sharp increase in the implied probability that Xi Jinping is removed from power before 2027 would signal acute CCP political instability, which maps most cleanly to a short-term risk-off selloff in liquid China equity proxies (FXI/KWEB) and a weaker offshore yuan. The equity channel is the strongest and could plausibly exceed the 700bps tradable threshold given the tail-risk nature of the event, but confidence is capped near coin-flip because most such probability moves are low-liquidity noise rather than genuine information leaks. The FX channel is directionally aligned but muted by PBOC management.
key_assumptions: The probability move is sharp and not already reflected in public headlines
A genuine Xi-removal signal would be interpreted as destabilizing, not stabilizing, in the immediate term
FXI/KWEB remain the most liquid and sensitive vehicles for expressing China political risk
Markets react before official confirmation, i.e., the prediction market can lead the tape
failure_modes: The probability spike is thin Polymarket noise or manipulation with no real information content — assets do not move
The event is already public/priced by the time the anomaly appears, so no residual asset move remains
The move reverses quickly once state media shows Xi in public, snapping FXI back up
Markets interpret potential succession as reform-friendly, flipping equities positive against the thesis
CYB proxy is too managed/illiquid to register the yuan move, understating the true FX reaction
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
